skills.name: Parent functions
skills.wrong_turn: √x and x² aren't the same curve: √x is only the right half of a parabola lying on its side, with domain x ≥ 0.
skills.rule: The parent functions: x, x2, x3, x, |x|, (1x), bx, logbx.

skills.name: Vertical shifts
skills.wrong_turn: y = x² − 3 moves down 3, not right 3. A number outside f moves the graph vertically.
skills.rule: y=f(x)+k shifts the graph of f up k units (down if k<0).

skills.name: Horizontal shifts
skills.wrong_turn: y = (x + 2)² moves left 2, not right 2. Where the inside equals 0 is the new vertex.
skills.rule: y=f(x−h) shifts the graph of f right h units (left if h<0).

skills.name: Reflections
skills.wrong_turn: −f(x) and f(−x) are different: for √x, −√x points down, √(−x) points left.
skills.rule: y=−f(x) reflects over the x-axis; y=f(−x) reflects over the y-axis.

skills.name: Vertical stretch & compress
skills.wrong_turn: 2f(x) doubles heights, not x-values: the zeros of 2f stay where f's zeros are.
skills.rule: y=af(x) stretches vertically by a if a>1 and compresses if 0<a<1.

skills.name: Horizontal stretch & compress
skills.wrong_turn: f(2x) is squeezed by half, not stretched by 2. The point (4, 2) on √x becomes (2, 2) on √(2x).
skills.rule: y=f(bx) compresses horizontally by a factor (1b) (for b>1) and stretches it for 0<b<1.

skills.name: Combined transformations
skills.wrong_turn: In √(2x − 6), the start is x = 3, not 6. Factor out the 2 first: √(2(x − 3)).
skills.rule: For y=af(b(x−h))+k, a point (x,y) of f goes to ((xb)+h,ay+k).

skills.name: Even & odd functions
skills.wrong_turn: Odd functions aren't those with odd numbers: x³ + 1 is not odd. Test f(−x) = −f(x).

skills.name: Symmetry of graphs

steps.d: use symmetry to finish a sketch

skills.wrong_turn: A function can't have x-axis symmetry unless it's y = 0: (x, y) and (x, −y) would give one input two outputs.
skills.rule: y-axis symmetry: (−x,y) is on the graph. Origin symmetry: (−x,−y) is. x-axis symmetry: (x,−y) is.

skills.name: End behavior
skills.wrong_turn: "f(x) → ∞" doesn't mean f reaches a number called infinity. It means f grows past every number.
skills.rule: End behaviour describes f(x) as x→∞ and x→−∞.

skills.name: Continuity informally
skills.wrong_turn: 1/x isn't "discontinuous at 0" in the usual sense: 0 isn't in its domain. It's continuous everywhere it's defined.
skills.rule: Informally, f is continuous if its graph has no jumps, holes or breaks.

skills.name: Asymptotes informally
skills.wrong_turn: A graph can cross its horizontal asymptote. The asymptote only describes what happens far out.
skills.rule: A vertical asymptote x=a is where f blows up; a horizontal asymptote y=L is a level f approaches at the ends.

skills.name: One-to-one & inverses on graphs
skills.wrong_turn: The vertical line test checks for a function; the horizontal line test checks for an inverse. Don't mix them up.
skills.rule: A function is one-to-one exactly when every horizontal line hits its graph at most once.

skills.name: Restrict a domain

steps.c: find the inverse on that piece

skills.wrong_turn: √(x²) is |x|, not x. On x ≤ 0, the inverse of x² is −√x.
skills.rule: Restrict the domain to a piece where f is one-to-one; then find the inverse on that piece.

skills.name: Composition on graphs & tables
skills.wrong_turn: For f(g(2)), start with g: look up g(2) first, then use it as f's input. Not f(2) first.
skills.rule: To find f(g(a)) from tables or graphs, find g(a), then look up f at that value.

skills.name: Choosing a model
skills.wrong_turn: Increasing by bigger amounts each time isn't enough for exponential. Check ratios: 1, 4, 9, 16 has ratios 4, 2.25, 1.78: quadratic.
skills.rule: Constant differences: linear. Constant second differences: quadratic. Constant ratios: exponential.

skills.name: Growth races
skills.wrong_turn: A bigger start doesn't win forever: 1000x beats 1.1^x for a long while, but 1.1^x still overtakes it eventually.
skills.rule: Any increasing exponential eventually exceeds any linear function, and any polynomial.

skills.name: Modulus graphs

steps.b: y = f(|x|) mirrors the right half

skills.wrong_turn: Don't mix up the two. y=f(|x|) copies the right half onto the left; it doesn't flip what is below the axis. For f(x)=x−2 at x=−5: f(|x|)=3, but |f(x)|=7.
skills.rule: y=|f(x)|: reflect the part below the x-axis up. y=f(|x|): drop the left half and mirror the right half.
